summary: Sprint 0 foundation (backend + CRA shim) fully verified. 12/12 backend pytest cases pass covering baseline meta routes, v1 meta/readiness, and the full auth scaffold (register, duplicate 409, login, wrong-password 401, refresh rotation with old-token revocation, logout). 8/8 Playwright UI flows pass covering landing, nav links, /login, /register, dashboard, duplicate-registration error surfacing, login → dashboard, and 404.

minor.issue: Not reachable through the public Emergent URL because ingress only forwards /api/* to the backend. Tests hit them via http://localhost:8001 to verify the contract, which matches how the pod is deployed. If external clients need them, they should be moved under /api/v1 (already present) or the ingress rules updated.

Shim ignores the Authorization header and returns the most recently registered user. Documented behavior in the shim comment, but will break multi-user QA scenarios. Canonical apps/api must implement real JWT validation before this endpoint is used by the UI.

issues: Input borders are extremely faint against the near-white background — accessibility contrast could be improved. Not blocking.

action_items: Sprint 0 acceptance criteria met — no fixes required.
Before Sprint 1: replace /app/backend/server.py shim with the canonical /app/apps/api implementation and wire real JWT validation for /auth/me (multi-user QA depends on it).
critical_code_review_comments: Shim /app/backend/server.py imports motor + connects to Mongo at startup but never uses it for auth persistence — either drop the Mongo client to reduce surface area or persist users/refresh tokens to Mongo so state survives supervisor restarts.
In-memory _users and _refresh_tokens dicts are lost on every backend restart; acceptable for Sprint 0 demo but must be flagged in the release notes to prevent QA confusion after redeploys.

/api/v1/auth/me returns 'most recently registered user' instead of validating the bearer token — this is a security smell even for a demo shim. Consider returning 501 Not Implemented until real JWT parsing lands.
JWT_SECRET falls back to a hardcoded string 'pod-shim-dev-secret' if env var is missing — fine for shim, but production apps/api must fail-fast when the secret is missing.
CORS allow_origins=['*'] combined with allow_credentials=True is invalid per CORS spec (browsers ignore credentials). Split allow-list explicitly for production.
test_credentials: Registered a fresh user per run: email=qa+agos-<uuid>@agrovix.dev, password=SprintZero!2026, full_name='AgOS QA'. See /app/memory/test_credentials.md.
seed_data_creation: None persisted — every test run registers a unique UUID-suffixed email so re-runs are hermetic. Note that the shim's in-memory store is wiped on backend restart.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend baseline routes (/, /health, /version) are only reachable via localhost:8001 in this pod — the Emergent ingress only routes /api/* publicly. Tests already handle this split. Auth is in-memory: if you restart supervisor between runs, previously-registered accounts vanish (this is expected for the shim). Canonical Postgres-backed API lives at /app/apps/api and is NOT the one served by supervisor.
